lanes.label: Elsewhere in scripture
lanes.range: Topics in other books wired to this one

nodes.t: Jesus is taken up and the apostles wait
nodes.d: Luke begins by recalling Jesus teaching the apostles for forty days, promising the Holy Ghost, and being taken up in a cloud. Two men in white say he will return in the same way, and the disciples return to Jerusalem to pray.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Jesus said before he went up into heaven and what the apostles did next?
ev: Retell what Jesus told the apostles to wait for and be witnesses of (1:4-8)
Say what the two men told the disciples about Jesus coming back (1:11)

nodes.t: Acts: overview
nodes.d: Acts continues Luke's account from the ascension of Jesus (1:9) to Paul preaching at Rome (28:31): the Holy Ghost at Pentecost, the church in Jerusalem, the witness spreading to Judaea, Samaria and the Gentiles, and Paul's journeys, arrest and voyage to Rome.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline how the gospel spreads in Acts from Jerusalem to Rome?
ev: Say how Acts 1:8 gives the shape of the book (Jerusalem, Judaea, Samaria, the uttermost part)
Name the major sections: Peter in Jerusalem, Stephen and Philip, Saul's conversion, Cornelius, Paul's journeys, Paul's arrest and Rome

nodes.t: Matthias takes the place of Judas
nodes.d: Peter says the scripture about Judas had to be fulfilled and that a witness of the resurrection must replace him. The group prays and the lot falls on Matthias, who is numbered with the eleven.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the believers chose a replacement for Judas and how they chose him?
ev: State the requirement Peter gives for the one to be chosen (1:21-22)
Explain how Matthias was chosen (1:23-26)

nodes.t: The Holy Ghost comes at Pentecost
nodes.d: On the day of Pentecost a sound like a rushing wind fills the house, tongues like fire rest on each of them, and they speak in other languages. Jews from many nations each hear the wonderful works of God in their own tongue, and some mock.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what happened at Pentecost and how the crowd responded?
ev: Describe the sound, the fire and the languages (2:2-4, 2:6-11)
Name the two reactions of the crowd (2:12-13)

nodes.t: Peter preaches at Pentecost
nodes.d: Peter says the outpouring is what Joel spoke of, declares that God raised the crucified Jesus and made him Lord and Christ, and calls on the hearers to repent and be baptized. About three thousand are added that day.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarise Peter's argument at Pentecost and what he told the people to do?
ev: Say how Peter uses Joel, and the Psalms of David, to explain Jesus (2:16-21, 2:25-35)
State what Peter tells the crowd to do and to whom the promise belongs (2:38-39)

nodes.t: The life of the first church
nodes.d: The new believers continue in the apostles' doctrine, fellowship, breaking of bread and prayers, share what they have with those in need, worship in the temple, and see the Lord add to the church daily.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what the first believers did together and how the church grew?
ev: List the four things the believers continued in (2:42)
Describe how they treated their possessions and each other (2:44-46)

nodes.t: The lame man at the Beautiful gate
nodes.d: Peter and John meet a man lame from birth begging at the temple gate. Peter commands him in the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth to rise and walk, and he enters the temple walking and praising God while the people look on in wonder.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the lame man was healed and in whose name it was done?
ev: Retell the healing, including what Peter said he did and did not have (3:6)
Describe how the people reacted (3:9-11)

nodes.t: Peter preaches in Solomon's porch
nodes.d: Peter tells the amazed crowd that the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob glorified his Son Jesus, whom they delivered up, and that faith in his name made the man strong. He calls them to repent so that their sins may be blotted out, and reminds them of God's covenant with the fathers and the blessing promised to Abraham's seed.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Peter said made the man walk and what he urged the crowd to do?
ev: Say whom Peter credits for the healing (3:12-16)
Explain what Peter calls the people to do and why (3:18-19, 3:25-26)

nodes.t: Peter and John before the council
nodes.d: The priests, the captain of the temple and the Sadducees arrest Peter and John, and about five thousand have believed. Filled with the Holy Ghost, Peter tells the rulers there is salvation in no other name than Jesus, and when ordered to stop speaking they answer that they cannot but speak what they have seen and heard.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Peter said to the rulers and why he and John would not stop preaching?
ev: State what Peter says about the name of Jesus (4:10-12)
Explain how Peter and John answered the order to stop (4:19-20)

nodes.t: The church prays for boldness
nodes.d: Released, Peter and John report to their own company, and together they pray to God the maker of heaven and earth, recalling that rulers gathered against his Christ according to his counsel. They ask for boldness, the place is shaken, and they are filled with the Holy Ghost.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the church prayed for after the threats and what happened next?
ev: Say what the believers asked God for (4:29-30)
Describe how God answered (4:31)

nodes.t: One heart and one soul: sharing with the needy
nodes.d: The multitude of believers are of one heart and soul, and owners of lands and houses sell them and lay the money at the apostles' feet for distribution to those in need. Joses, called Barnabas, is named as one who sold land and gave the money.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe how the early believers shared and who Barnabas was?
ev: Describe how the believers met one another's needs (4:34-35)
Name the man given as an example and what he did (4:36-37)

nodes.t: Ananias and Sapphira
nodes.d: Ananias and Sapphira sell a possession and keep back part of the price while laying the rest at the apostles' feet. Peter says they lied to the Holy Ghost and to God; both fall down dead and great fear comes on the church.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Ananias and Sapphira did wrong and what happened?
ev: Say what the couple did and what Peter said it really was (5:2-4, 5:9)
Describe the effect on the church (5:11)

nodes.t: The apostles freed and brought before the council
nodes.d: Many signs are done and multitudes are healed, so the high priest and Sadducees imprison the apostles. An angel of the Lord opens the prison and sends them back to teach in the temple; before the council they say they must obey God rather than men, Gamaliel advises caution, and they leave rejoicing and keep teaching Jesus Christ.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the apostles escaped prison and why they kept preaching after being beaten?
ev: Describe how the apostles were freed and what the angel told them (5:19-20)
Summarise Gamaliel's advice and the apostles' response (5:29, 5:38-42)

nodes.t: Seven men are chosen to serve
nodes.d: When Grecian widows are neglected in the daily distribution, the twelve ask the disciples to choose seven men of good report, full of the Holy Ghost and wisdom, so that the apostles can give themselves to prayer and the word. Stephen and six others are chosen and prayed for, and the word of God increases.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the seven were chosen and what the apostles kept doing?
ev: Say what problem arose and what the apostles proposed (6:1-4)
Name the first of the seven chosen (6:5)

nodes.t: Stephen is seized and accused
nodes.d: Stephen, full of faith and power, does wonders among the people; men from several synagogues dispute with him and cannot resist his wisdom. They bring false witnesses before the council who say he spoke against the temple and Moses' customs, and the council sees his face like the face of an angel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Stephen was accused of and who accused him?
ev: State the charges brought against Stephen (6:11-14)
Describe how the council saw Stephen (6:15)

nodes.t: Stephen's speech: Abraham, the patriarchs and Joseph
nodes.d: Asked by the high priest if the charges are true, Stephen begins with the God of glory appearing to Abraham, the promise of the land, the covenant of circumcision and the sons of Jacob. He tells how the patriarchs sold Joseph in envy, yet God was with him and raised him up in Egypt, and how Jacob and his family came down there.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline how Stephen begins his speech from Abraham to Joseph?
ev: Say what God promised Abraham and how long his seed would be in a strange land (7:3-7)
Retell what Stephen says about Joseph and his brothers (7:9-14)

nodes.t: Stephen's speech: Moses and the people's refusal
nodes.d: Stephen recounts Israel's growth in Egypt, the birth and upbringing of Moses, his first attempt to help his brethren and their rejection, and God's call from the burning bush. He says the people refused Moses, turned back in their hearts to Egypt, and made a calf.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Stephen says Israel treated Moses, whom God sent as ruler and deliverer?
ev: Retell the stages of Moses' life Stephen names (7:20-36)
Say how Stephen says the fathers treated Moses (7:35, 7:39-41)

nodes.t: Stephen's speech: tabernacle, temple and stiffnecked people
nodes.d: Stephen recalls the tabernacle in the wilderness and David and Solomon's house, then says the Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands. He charges the council with resisting the Holy Ghost like their fathers, who persecuted the prophets and now betrayed and murdered the Just One.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Stephen answers the charge about the temple and what he accuses the council of?
ev: Say what Stephen says about where God dwells (7:48-50)
State the charge Stephen makes against the council (7:51-53)

nodes.t: Stephen sees Jesus and is stoned
nodes.d: The council is cut to the heart, but Stephen, full of the Holy Ghost, sees the glory of God and Jesus standing at God's right hand. They stone him outside the city, with the witnesses laying their clothes at the feet of a young man named Saul, and Stephen prays that the Lord Jesus receive his spirit and that this sin not be laid to their charge.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Stephen saw, how he died, and what he asked for his killers?
ev: Say what Stephen saw and said before he died (7:55-56)
Give his two prayers as he was stoned (7:59-60)

nodes.t: Persecution scatters the church
nodes.d: Saul consents to Stephen's death and a great persecution scatters the church in Jerusalem throughout Judaea and Samaria, except the apostles. Saul ravages the church, entering houses and imprisoning men and women, while the scattered believers go everywhere preaching the word.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how the persecution after Stephen spread the word?
ev: Say what Saul did to the church (8:3)
Explain what the scattered believers did (8:4)

nodes.t: Philip in Samaria and Simon the sorcerer
nodes.d: Philip preaches Christ in Samaria with miracles, and many believe and are baptized, including Simon who had practised sorcery. Peter and John come, pray, and lay hands on them so they receive the Holy Ghost; when Simon offers money for this power, Peter rebukes him and tells him to repent.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Philip did in Samaria and why Peter rebuked Simon?
ev: Describe what happened in Samaria through Philip (8:5-8, 8:12)
Explain why Peter rebuked Simon (8:18-23)

nodes.t: Philip and the Ethiopian eunuch
nodes.d: An angel and the Spirit send Philip to a chariot on the road to Gaza, where an Ethiopian officer is reading Isaiah. Philip begins at that scripture and preaches Jesus; the man believes, is baptized, and goes on his way rejoicing.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell how Philip explained the scripture to the Ethiopian and what happened afterward?
ev: Say what the eunuch was reading and what Philip did with it (8:28-35)
Describe the baptism and what happened to Philip (8:36-40)

nodes.t: Saul meets Jesus on the road to Damascus
nodes.d: Saul, breathing threats against the disciples, is stopped near Damascus by a light from heaven and the voice of Jesus asking why he persecutes him. Struck blind, he is led into the city, and Ananias, sent by the Lord, lays hands on him; he receives sight, is filled with the Holy Ghost, and is baptized.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to Saul on the Damascus road and how Ananias helped him?
ev: Say what Jesus said to Saul and what Saul asked (9:4-6)
Explain what the Lord told Ananias about Saul (9:15-16)

nodes.t: Saul preaches and escapes from Damascus
nodes.d: Saul immediately preaches in the synagogues that Jesus is the Son of God, and the Jews plot to kill him, so the disciples let him down the wall in a basket. In Jerusalem Barnabas brings him to the apostles, and when the Grecians try to kill him he is sent to Tarsus while the churches have rest.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Saul was accepted by the disciples in Jerusalem?
ev: Describe how Saul escaped Damascus (9:23-25)
Say what Barnabas did for Saul (9:26-27)

nodes.t: Peter heals Aeneas and raises Dorcas
nodes.d: Peter heals the paralysed Aeneas at Lydda in the name of Jesus Christ and many turn to the Lord. At Joppa he kneels, prays, and says "Tabitha, arise" to the disciple Dorcas, who is presented alive, and many believe.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell the stories of Aeneas and Dorcas and what people did afterward?
ev: Describe the two miracles Peter did (9:34, 9:40)
Say what Dorcas was known for (9:36, 9:39)

nodes.t: Cornelius and Peter see visions
nodes.d: Cornelius, a devout centurion at Caesarea, is told by an angel to send for Simon Peter at Joppa. Meanwhile Peter sees a sheet of animals let down from heaven and is told what God has cleansed not to call common, and the Spirit tells him to go with the three men.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the two visions and how they brought Peter and Cornelius together?
ev: Describe Cornelius' vision and what he did (10:3-8)
Say what the voice told Peter and what it meant for his actions (10:13-20)

nodes.t: Peter preaches to Cornelius and the Gentiles receive the Spirit
nodes.d: Peter tells Cornelius' household that God is no respecter of persons and that everyone who believes in Jesus receives remission of sins. While he is speaking the Holy Ghost falls on the Gentiles, and Peter commands them to be baptized.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Peter preached to Cornelius and why he baptized the Gentiles?
ev: State what Peter says about God and every nation (10:34-35)
Explain why Peter orders the Gentiles to be baptized (10:44-48)

nodes.t: Peter explains himself in Jerusalem
nodes.d: Believers in Judaea criticise Peter for eating with uncircumcised men, so he retells the vision and the Spirit falling on the Gentiles. Hearing it, they glorify God and say he has granted repentance unto life to the Gentiles also.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Peter answered those who criticised him about the Gentiles?
ev: Say what the believers objected to (11:2-3)
State the conclusion the church reached (11:17-18)

nodes.t: The church at Antioch and the first Christians
nodes.d: Scattered believers preach the Lord Jesus to Greeks at Antioch and a great number believe; Barnabas is sent, finds Saul at Tarsus, and they teach there a year, where the disciples are first called Christians. The Antioch disciples send relief to Judaea after Agabus foretells a famine.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the Antioch church began and what it did for the brethren in Judaea?
ev: Say where the disciples were first called Christians (11:26)
Describe what the Antioch church did when famine was foretold (11:27-30)

nodes.t: James killed and Peter freed from prison
nodes.d: Herod kills James and imprisons Peter, but the church prays unceasingly. An angel leads Peter out past the guards at night, and he comes to the house of Mary, where Rhoda is so glad she forgets to open the gate and the astonished believers at last let him in.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how God rescued Peter and what the church was doing at the time?
ev: Describe how Peter was brought out of prison (12:6-10)
Say what the church was doing and how they reacted (12:5, 12:12-16)

nodes.t: Herod's death and the word of God grows
nodes.d: Herod, in royal apparel, receives the people's shout that he speaks as a god; the angel of the Lord strikes him because he gave not God the glory. The word of God grows and multiplies, and Barnabas and Saul return with John Mark.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Herod died and what happened to the word of God?
ev: Say why Herod was struck down (12:22-23)
Contrast Herod's end with what happened to the word of God (12:24)

nodes.t: Barnabas and Saul are sent out from Antioch
nodes.d: The Holy Ghost tells the Antioch prophets and teachers to separate Barnabas and Saul for the work, and the church fasts, prays and sends them. On Cyprus, Saul (also called Paul) strikes the sorcerer Elymas blind and the deputy Sergius Paulus believes.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who sent Barnabas and Saul out and what happened on Cyprus?
ev: Say how Barnabas and Saul were sent (13:2-4)
Describe what happened to Elymas and the deputy (13:8-12)

nodes.t: Paul preaches in the synagogue at Pisidian Antioch
nodes.d: Invited to speak after the reading of the law and prophets, Paul traces Israel's story from Egypt through the judges and David to Jesus, whom God raised from the dead. He declares forgiveness of sins and that by Jesus all who believe are justified from what the law of Moses could not justify.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarise Paul's sermon from Israel's history to forgiveness through Jesus?
ev: Outline the history Paul recounts to reach Jesus (13:17-23)
State what Paul says is preached through Jesus (13:38-39)

nodes.t: Paul and Barnabas turn to the Gentiles
nodes.d: Gentiles ask to hear more, and the next sabbath almost the whole city gathers; the envious Jews contradict, so Paul and Barnabas say they turn to the Gentiles, citing the Lord's command to be a light to them. The Gentiles rejoice, those ordained to eternal life believe, and the apostles are expelled.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul and Barnabas turned to the Gentiles at Antioch?
ev: Say why Paul and Barnabas turned to the Gentiles (13:45-47)
Describe how the Gentiles and the disciples responded (13:48, 13:52)

nodes.t: Iconium and Lystra: healing, worship refused, stoning
nodes.d: At Iconium many believe but the city is divided and the apostles flee. At Lystra Paul heals a man lame from birth and the crowd calls them gods; the apostles stop the sacrifice and preach the living God who made heaven and earth, but Jews from Antioch and Iconium turn the people and stone Paul, who rises up and goes on.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened at Lystra and what the apostles said to the crowd?
ev: Say how Paul and Barnabas responded when the people wanted to sacrifice to them (14:14-18)
Describe what happened to Paul after the healing (14:19-20)

nodes.t: The return to Antioch: elders appointed
nodes.d: Paul and Barnabas return through the cities, confirming the disciples, warning that entering the kingdom is through much tribulation, and ordaining elders in every church with prayer and fasting. Back at Antioch they report that God had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul and Barnabas did on their way back and what they reported?
ev: Say what the apostles told the disciples about tribulation (14:22)
Describe the report given at Antioch (14:26-27)

nodes.t: The Jerusalem council on circumcision
nodes.d: Men from Judaea teach that Gentiles must be circumcised to be saved, so Paul and Barnabas go to Jerusalem. Peter recalls God giving the Gentiles the Holy Ghost and says salvation is through the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ; James cites the prophets and judges that Gentile believers should not be troubled, only asked to abstain from idols, fornication, strangled things and blood.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the question the Jerusalem council settled and how they answered it?
ev: State the question that began the dispute (15:1, 15:5)
Say what Peter and James each concluded (15:7-11, 15:13-19)

nodes.t: The letter to the Gentile churches
nodes.d: The apostles and elders send Judas Barsabas and Silas with Paul and Barnabas, carrying a letter saying that it seemed good to the Holy Ghost and to them to lay no greater burden than the necessary things. The Antioch believers read it and rejoice.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the letter from Jerusalem said and how Antioch responded?
ev: Say who delivered the letter and what it asked of Gentile believers (15:22-29)
Describe how Antioch received it (15:30-32)

nodes.t: Paul and Barnabas part ways
nodes.d: Paul proposes revisiting the churches, and Barnabas wants to take John Mark, whom Paul will not take since he left them in Pamphylia. The contention is so sharp that they separate; Barnabas takes Mark to Cyprus and Paul takes Silas through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why Paul and Barnabas separated and who went with each?
ev: Say what the disagreement was about (15:37-38)
Describe where each pair went (15:39-41)

nodes.t: Timothy joins and the call to Macedonia
nodes.d: At Lystra Paul takes Timothy, whose mother is a believing Jewess and whose father is Greek, and circumcises him because of the Jews there, while delivering the Jerusalem decrees. Forbidden by the Spirit to go to Asia or Bithynia, Paul sees a vision of a man of Macedonia and concludes the Lord has called them to preach there.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul was led to go to Macedonia?
ev: Say why Paul circumcised Timothy (16:3)
Describe how the Spirit directed the journey (16:6-10)

nodes.t: Lydia's heart is opened at Philippi
nodes.d: At Philippi on the sabbath Paul speaks to women by the river, and the Lord opens the heart of Lydia, a seller of purple who worshipped God. She and her household are baptized, and she constrains the missionaries to stay in her house.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Lydia came to believe at Philippi?
ev: Say who Lydia was and how she came to believe (16:14)
Describe what she did after being baptized (16:15)

nodes.t: Paul and Silas in the Philippian jail
nodes.d: After Paul casts a spirit out of a slave girl, her owners have Paul and Silas beaten and jailed. At midnight they pray and sing, an earthquake opens the doors, and the jailer asks what he must do to be saved; they tell him to believe on the Lord Jesus Christ, and he and his household are baptized.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened in the Philippian jail and how the jailer was saved?
ev: Describe what Paul and Silas did in the prison at midnight (16:25)
Give the jailer's question and the answer (16:30-31)

nodes.t: Paul insists on his rights as a Roman
nodes.d: The magistrates send word to let Paul and Silas go, but Paul says they were beaten openly uncondemned, being Romans, and demands that the magistrates come themselves. The magistrates fear and ask them to leave, and the pair visit Lydia's house and encourage the brethren before departing.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul would not leave the Philippian prison quietly?
ev: Say what Paul demanded and why (16:37)
Describe the magistrates' reaction (16:38-39)

nodes.t: Thessalonica and Berea: reasoning from the scriptures
nodes.d: At Thessalonica Paul reasons from the scriptures for three sabbaths that Christ must suffer and rise again; some believe but jealous Jews raise an uproar against Jason's house. At Berea the Jews receive the word readily and search the scriptures daily to see whether these things are so, but opponents from Thessalonica follow.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the Bereans did with Paul's message?
ev: Say what Paul argued from the scriptures (17:2-3)
Explain what made the Bereans noble (17:11)

nodes.t: Paul at the Areopagus in Athens
nodes.d: Distressed by the idols of Athens, Paul is brought to the Areopagus, where he speaks of the altar to the unknown God. He says God who made the world does not dwell in temples, gave life and breath to all, made all nations of one blood, commands all men to repent, and will judge the world by the man he raised from the dead; some mock, and some believe.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} summarise what Paul said to the Athenians about God, repentance and judgment?
ev: Say what Paul tells the Athenians about the God who made the world (17:24-28)
State the command and the warning in 17:30-31

nodes.t: Paul at Corinth
nodes.d: At Corinth Paul works with Aquila and Priscilla and reasons in the synagogue; when the Jews oppose, he goes to the Gentiles, and Crispus the synagogue ruler believes. The Lord tells him in a night vision not to be afraid, for he has much people in the city, and Gallio dismisses the Jews' charge against him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to Paul at Corinth and what the Lord told him?
ev: Say what the Lord told Paul in the night (18:9-10)
Describe how Gallio handled the accusation (18:14-16)

nodes.t: Apollos is taught more perfectly
nodes.d: Paul sails to Ephesus, Caesarea and Antioch and then strengthens the disciples in Galatia and Phrygia. Apollos, an eloquent man mighty in the scriptures who knows only the baptism of John, is taken aside by Aquila and Priscilla, who expound the way of God to him more perfectly, and he helps the believers in Achaia.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Apollos was helped by Priscilla and Aquila?
ev: Say what Apollos knew and lacked (18:24-25)
Describe what Aquila and Priscilla did for him (18:26)

nodes.t: Paul at Ephesus: the twelve disciples and the school of Tyrannus
nodes.d: Paul finds about twelve disciples at Ephesus who know only John's baptism; they are baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus, and when Paul lays hands on them the Holy Ghost comes and they speak with tongues and prophesy. Paul then reasons for two years, so that all in Asia hear the word of the Lord Jesus.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to the twelve disciples at Ephesus?
ev: Say what the disciples had and had not received (19:2-5)
Describe where and how long Paul taught after leaving the synagogue (19:9-10)

nodes.t: Miracles at Ephesus and the burning of the books
nodes.d: God works special miracles through Paul, and the seven sons of Sceva who try to use the name of Jesus over an evil spirit are overpowered. Fear falls on Ephesus, the name of the Lord Jesus is magnified, and believers burn their magic books worth fifty thousand pieces of silver.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to the sons of Sceva and what the believers did with their books?
ev: Say what happened to the sons of Sceva (19:13-16)
Describe how the believers responded (19:17-19)

nodes.t: The riot of the silversmiths at Ephesus
nodes.d: Demetrius the silversmith, whose trade in shrines for Diana is threatened by Paul's teaching that gods made with hands are no gods, stirs up the craftsmen. The whole city rushes into the theatre shouting "Great is Diana", until the town clerk quiets the crowd and says that disputes belong to the law courts and a lawful assembly.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why the craftsmen at Ephesus were angry and how the riot ended?
ev: Say what Demetrius said was at stake (19:24-27)
Explain how the town clerk calmed the crowd (19:35-41)

nodes.t: Eutychus falls from the window at Troas
nodes.d: Paul travels through Macedonia and Greece to Troas, where the disciples meet on the first day of the week to break bread. Paul speaks until midnight, young Eutychus falls from a third-floor window and is taken up dead, and Paul embraces him and tells them his life is in him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell what happened to Eutychus while Paul was preaching?
ev: Describe what happened to Eutychus (20:9-10)
Say what the disciples were doing when Paul preached (20:7)

nodes.t: Paul's farewell to the Ephesian elders
nodes.d: At Miletus Paul calls the Ephesian elders and recalls his service and teaching in Asia, telling them he goes bound in the Spirit to Jerusalem. He charges them to feed the church of God, warns of grievous wolves arising even from among them, commends them to God and the word of his grace, and recalls that it is more blessed to give than to receive.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain Paul's charge to the Ephesian elders and the warnings he gave?
ev: Say what Paul told the elders to do and why (20:28-31)
Describe how the elders and Paul parted (20:36-38)

nodes.t: Warnings along the road to Jerusalem
nodes.d: Paul sails to Tyre, where disciples tell him through the Spirit not to go up to Jerusalem, and stays at Caesarea with Philip the evangelist. The prophet Agabus binds his own hands and feet with Paul's girdle and says the Jews will bind him; Paul replies that he is ready to die for the name of the Lord Jesus, and they say the will of the Lord be done.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the warnings Paul received on his way to Jerusalem and how he answered?
ev: Say what Agabus did and said (21:10-11)
Explain Paul's answer to those who begged him not to go (21:13-14)

nodes.t: Paul and the vow in the temple
nodes.d: At Jerusalem James and the elders glorify God for Paul's report, but tell him that thousands of Jews zealous for the law have heard he teaches against Moses. They advise him to join four men with a vow, and restate that Gentile believers need keep only the things in the earlier letter; Paul does so in the temple.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why James and the elders advised Paul to take part in the vow?
ev: Say what rumour the elders mention and what they advised (21:20-24)
Restate the instruction about Gentile believers (21:25)

nodes.t: Paul is seized in the temple and arrested
nodes.d: Jews from Asia stir up the people against Paul, saying he teaches against the people, the law and the place and has brought Greeks into the temple. They drag him out to kill him, the chief captain rescues him and binds him with chains, and Paul asks leave to speak to the people.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why Paul was seized in the temple and how he was rescued?
ev: Describe the charges of the Asian Jews (21:28-29)
Say how Paul was saved from the mob (21:31-33)

nodes.t: Paul tells his story to the crowd
nodes.d: Speaking in Hebrew from the stairs, Paul tells of his upbringing under Gamaliel, his persecution of the Way, the vision on the Damascus road, and Ananias' words. He says that in the temple the Lord told him to depart because he would be sent far to the Gentiles, and at that word the crowd cries out for his death.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Paul's own account of how he came to follow Jesus and why the crowd shouted?
ev: Summarise the parts of his life Paul describes (22:3-5, 22:6-16)
Say which word made the crowd shout (22:21-22)

nodes.t: Paul declares he is a Roman
nodes.d: As the chief captain orders Paul to be examined by scourging, Paul asks the centurion whether it is lawful to scourge a Roman uncondemned. The chief captain is afraid on learning that Paul is a Roman, freeborn, and next day sets him before the chief priests and council.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul's Roman citizenship affected his treatment?
ev: Say what Paul asked the centurion (22:25)
Describe how the chief captain reacted (22:26-29)

nodes.t: Paul before the council: the resurrection
nodes.d: Paul tells the council he has lived in all good conscience, and when the high priest orders him struck, he rebukes him and then says he did not know he was the high priest. Perceiving Sadducees and Pharisees, he says he is called in question for the hope of the resurrection, the council divides, and the Lord stands by him that night to say he must bear witness at Rome.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul used the question of the resurrection before the council?
ev: Say how Paul divided the council (23:6-9)
State what the Lord told Paul that night (23:11)

nodes.t: The plot against Paul and his transfer to Caesarea
nodes.d: More than forty Jews bind themselves by a curse to neither eat nor drink till they have killed Paul. Paul's sister's son tells the chief captain, who sends Paul by night with a large escort and a letter to Felix at Caesarea.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the plot against Paul was discovered and how he was kept safe?
ev: Describe the plot and who uncovered it (23:12-16)
Say what the chief captain's letter reports (23:26-30)

nodes.t: Paul before Felix
nodes.d: The high priest and the orator Tertullus accuse Paul before Felix; Paul answers that he worships the God of his fathers, believes the law and the prophets, and hopes for a resurrection of the just and unjust. Felix trembles when Paul reasons of righteousness, temperance and judgment to come, but defers him and leaves him bound for two years.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul defended himself before Felix and how Felix responded?
ev: Say what Paul confessed about the way he worships (24:14-16)
Describe Felix's response and how long Paul stayed bound (24:25-27)

nodes.t: Paul appeals to Caesar
nodes.d: Festus succeeds Felix and the Jews ask that Paul be sent to Jerusalem, intending an ambush. Paul says he has not offended against the law, the temple or Caesar, refuses to be handed over, and appeals to Caesar; Festus answers that he will go to Caesar.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Paul appealed to Caesar?
ev: Say what Paul said when Festus proposed a trial at Jerusalem (25:9-11)
Give Festus' decision (25:12)

nodes.t: Festus lays Paul's case before King Agrippa
nodes.d: King Agrippa and Bernice visit Festus, who explains that the accusers brought no charge he expected, only questions about their religion and about one Jesus who was dead whom Paul affirmed to be alive. Agrippa wishes to hear Paul and Festus brings him forth, saying he has no certain thing to write to Caesar.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Festus told Agrippa about Paul's case?
ev: Say how Festus summarised the case (25:18-19)
State why Festus brought Paul before Agrippa (25:26-27)

nodes.t: Paul's defence before Agrippa
nodes.d: Paul tells Agrippa of his life as a Pharisee, his persecution of the saints and the vision on the road to Damascus, where Jesus sends him to open eyes and turn Gentiles from darkness to light. He says he says nothing beyond what Moses and the prophets said, that Christ should suffer and rise first, and Agrippa answers "Almost thou persuadest me to be a Christian".
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Paul's speech to Agrippa and how Agrippa replied?
ev: State the commission Jesus gave Paul (26:16-18)
Say what Paul says the prophets and Moses foretold (26:22-23)

nodes.t: The voyage to Rome and the storm
nodes.d: Paul and other prisoners are delivered to the centurion Julius and sail for Italy; Paul warns of danger but the centurion trusts the master of the ship. A tempest drives the ship for many days until all hope is lost, then an angel tells Paul he must stand before Caesar and that God has given him all who sail with him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how the storm began and what God told Paul in it?
ev: Say what Paul warned and who was believed (27:9-11)
Give the angel's message to Paul (27:23-25)

nodes.t: The shipwreck and the escape to land
nodes.d: On the fourteenth night the sailors try to flee and Paul tells the centurion they must stay in the ship; Paul urges all to eat and gives thanks to God before them. The ship runs aground and breaks up, the centurion stops the soldiers from killing the prisoners, and all 276 reach land safe.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how everyone on the ship came safely to land?
ev: Describe what Paul urged before the wreck (27:31, 27:33-36)
Say what happened to the people on board (27:42-44)

nodes.t: Paul on Malta
nodes.d: The islanders show kindness; when a viper fastens on Paul's hand he shakes it off unharmed, and they change their minds and say he is a god. Paul prays for and heals the father of Publius and others on the island.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened to Paul on Malta?
ev: Describe the viper and the islanders' two opinions (28:3-6)
Say what Paul did for Publius' father (28:8)

nodes.t: Paul arrives at Rome
nodes.d: After three months the party sails in a ship of Alexandria and lands at Puteoli, where they find brethren. Believers from Rome come to meet Paul on the road, and he thanks God and takes courage; at Rome he is allowed to dwell by himself with a soldier.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Paul arrived at Rome and who welcomed him?
ev: Say how the Roman brethren met Paul (28:15)
Describe the conditions of his stay at Rome (28:16)

nodes.t: Paul preaches in Rome
nodes.d: Paul tells the Jewish leaders at Rome that he is bound for the hope of Israel and expounds the kingdom of God from Moses and the prophets, with some believing and others not. He quotes Isaiah on hardened hearts, says salvation is sent to the Gentiles, and for two years receives all who come, preaching with all confidence, no man forbidding him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Paul did and said at Rome and how Acts ends?
ev: Say how the Jews divided in response (28:24-25)
Describe how the book ends (28:30-31)

nodes.t: Genesis: overview
nodes.d: Genesis runs from creation (1:1) to the death of Joseph in Egypt (50:26): creation, the fall, the flood, Babel, and the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and Joseph.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Genesis in order, from creation to Joseph in Egypt?
ev: Name the four main sections: creation, fall and flood, Abraham, and the patriarchs through Joseph
Say where the story begins (1:1) and ends (50:26)

nodes.t: God calls Abram
nodes.d: God calls Abram to leave his country and promises to make him a great nation and bless all the families of the earth through him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} list what God promised Abram in Genesis 12:1-3?
ev: State the promises of 12:1-3
Say that Abram went as the LORD told him

nodes.t: God's covenant with Abram
nodes.d: God confirms his promise of offspring and land to Abram and makes a covenant with him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what God promised Abram in Genesis 15 and how Abram responded?
ev: Describe the promises of offspring and land
Read 15:6 and say what Abram believed

nodes.t: The sign of circumcision
nodes.d: God appears to Abram at ninety-nine, changes his name to Abraham, and gives circumcision as the sign of the covenant.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what circumcision was a sign of in Genesis 17?
ev: Explain the name change (17:5)
State what circumcision signified (17:10-11)

nodes.t: Abraham offers Isaac
nodes.d: God tests Abraham by commanding him to offer Isaac; God provides a ram in his place.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what God provided on the mountain?
ev: Retell the story, including 22:8 and 22:13-14

nodes.t: Joseph is sold by his brothers
nodes.d: Joseph's brothers hate him and sell him to traders who take him to Egypt.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell why Joseph's brothers sold him?
ev: Retell the story from the dreams to the sale

nodes.t: Joseph is raised up in Egypt
nodes.d: Joseph interprets Pharaoh's dreams and is set over the land of Egypt.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell how Joseph came to rule in Egypt?
ev: Retell the dreams and what Joseph advised

nodes.t: Jacob goes down to Egypt
nodes.d: At Beersheba God tells Israel not to fear going down into Egypt, promising to make him a great nation there, go down with him and bring him up again. The household that came into Egypt is listed, and Joseph meets his father in Goshen and prepares them to speak to Pharaoh as shepherds.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what God promised Jacob before he went down to Egypt?
ev: State God's three promises to Jacob in 46:3-4
Give the total number of Jacob's house who came into Egypt (46:26-27)

nodes.t: Exodus: overview
nodes.d: Exodus tells of Israel enslaved in Egypt (1:1-14) and delivered through the plagues, Passover and the sea (chapters 7-15), then of the covenant at Sinai (19-24) and the tabernacle (25-40), ending with the glory of the LORD filling it (40:34-38).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Exodus in order, from the bondage in Egypt to the glory filling the tabernacle?
ev: Name the main sections: bondage, deliverance, the journey to Sinai, the law and covenant, and the tabernacle
Say where Exodus begins (1:1) and ends (40:38)

nodes.t: Moses flees to Midian and God hears Israel's cry
nodes.d: Grown up, Moses kills an Egyptian who was beating a Hebrew, learns the deed is known, and flees to Midian, where he helps the priest's daughters and marries Zipporah. In Egypt the people groan, and God hears and remembers his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain why Moses ended up in Midian, and what 2:23-25 says God did about Israel's cry?
ev: Say why Moses left Egypt (2:11-15)
Say what Moses did at the well in Midian (2:16-17)
Find the verse that says God remembered his covenant (2:24)

nodes.t: The burning bush
nodes.d: While keeping Jethro's flock at Horeb, Moses sees a bush burning without being consumed. God calls him by name from it, declares the ground holy, identifies himself as the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, and says he has seen Israel's affliction and will send Moses to Pharaoh.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what happened at the burning bush and what God said to Moses there?
ev: Describe what Moses saw and what God told him to do with his shoes (3:2-5)
Say what God said he had seen and heard (3:7-9)
Say what God sent Moses to do (3:10)

nodes.t: Judgments: purity, the poor and the stranger
nodes.d: Laws cover seduction of a maid, sorcery, sacrificing to another god, and care for strangers, widows, the fatherless and the poor, whom Israel must not oppress because they themselves were strangers in Egypt. Firstfruits and the firstborn are to be given to the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what 22:21-27 says about strangers, widows and the poor and why?
ev: Say how strangers, widows and orphans were to be treated and why (22:21-24)
Say what was to be done with a neighbour's pledged cloak (22:26-27)

nodes.t: The golden calf
nodes.d: When Moses delays on the mountain, the people ask Aaron to make gods for them. Aaron collects their gold earrings and fashions a molten calf, builds an altar and proclaims a feast, and the people offer sacrifices and rise up to play.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what the people did while Moses was on the mountain?
ev: Say what the people asked and what Aaron made (32:1-4)
Say what Aaron proclaimed (32:5)

nodes.t: A prophet like Moses
nodes.d: Deuteronomy 18:15-22 promises that the LORD will raise up a prophet like Moses from among his brothers, recalls Israel's request at Horeb not to hear the LORD's voice directly, puts the LORD's words in the prophet's mouth, and gives a test for false prophets.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD promised in Deuteronomy 18:15-19 and how to tell a false prophet?
ev: Say what the LORD promises in 18:15 and 18:18.
Give the test of 18:22 for a prophet who speaks in the LORD's name.

nodes.t: Psalms: overview
nodes.d: The Psalms are 150 songs and prayers addressed to or about the LORD: cries for help, confession, thanksgiving, praise of his creation and rule, songs about the king, and meditation on his law; the book closes with calls to praise (146-150).
nodes.q: Can {{name}} name three kinds of psalm and read one verse from a psalm of each kind?
ev: Name several kinds of psalm (lament, thanksgiving, praise, royal, wisdom) and give one psalm number for each.

nodes.t: Psalm 2: the nations rage, the LORD’s king is set on Zion
nodes.d: The kings of the earth set themselves against the LORD and his anointed, the LORD laughs and says he has set his king on Zion, declares him his Son, and warns the kings to serve the LORD with fear.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} outline Psalm 2 in its four parts and say what the kings are warned to do?
ev: List who rages against whom (2:1-3), who answers (2:4-6), and what the kings are told to do (2:10-12).

nodes.t: Psalm 16: the LORD is my portion and I will not be moved
nodes.d: The speaker takes refuge in the LORD, calls him his portion and cup, sets him always before him, and expects his heart to be glad and his soul not left in hell, with fulness of joy and pleasures at God’s right hand.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the speaker says in Psalm 16:8-11 about the LORD’s presence?
ev: Read 16:5-11 and list the reasons the speaker rejoices.

nodes.t: Psalm 69: zeal for thy house; they gave me vinegar
nodes.d: The speaker is sinking in deep waters and hated without cause, says zeal for God’s house has consumed him and reproaches have fallen on him, that he was given gall and vinegar, asks that his adversaries’ table be a snare and their eyes darkened, and ends with praise.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the suffering in Psalm 69:1-4 and 69:20-21 and how the psalm ends?
ev: Read 69:1-4, 69:9, 69:21 and 69:22-28 and list what the speaker suffers and asks.

nodes.t: Psalm 109: a cry against false accusers
nodes.d: The speaker says the wicked speak against him with lying tongues and repay evil for love, and prays that the accuser’s days be few and his reward come from the LORD; he says he is poor and needy and asks God to save him.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Psalm 109 moves from the speaker’s complaint to his prayer for help?
ev: Read 109:1-5, 109:6-20 and 109:21-31 and note how the psalm moves from complaint to curse to appeal.

nodes.t: Psalm 110: sit at my right hand; a priest after Melchizedek
nodes.d: The LORD says to the speaker’s Lord to sit at his right hand until his enemies are his footstool; he is a king sent to rule from Zion and a priest for ever after the order of Melchizedek, sworn by the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} read Psalm 110:1 and 110:4 and say what the LORD says to the speaker’s Lord?
ev: Read 110:1-4 and say who speaks and to whom, and what is sworn.

nodes.t: Psalms 117-118: his mercy endureth for ever; the stone the builders refused
nodes.d: Psalm 117 calls all nations to praise the LORD for his great mercy and truth; Psalm 118 calls Israel to say his mercy endures for ever, tells of being delivered from distress, says it is better to trust the LORD than man, speaks of the stone the builders refused, and ends with giving thanks.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain the refrain “his mercy endureth for ever” and the picture in Psalm 118:22-23?
ev: Read 118:5-9, 118:19-24 and 118:26-29 and list what is said about the LORD and the gate.

nodes.t: Psalm 132: the LORD’s oath to David and his choice of Zion
nodes.d: The psalm recalls David’s vow to find a dwelling for the LORD and says the LORD swore to David that his seed would sit on his throne if his children keep his covenant; the LORD chose Zion for his rest and will make the horn of David to bud.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what Psalm 132:11-12 says the LORD swore to David?
ev: Read 132:11-18 and say what the LORD swore and what he chose.

nodes.t: Isaiah: overview
nodes.d: Isaiah son of Amoz sees visions concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah; the book moves from indictment and judgment to comfort, a servant, and new heavens and a new earth.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who Isaiah was and describe, using Isaiah 1:1 and 40:1-2, how the book moves from rebuke to comfort?
ev: Name the four kings of Judah named in Isaiah 1:1
Describe the shift in tone between chapters 1-39 and chapter 40 using the texts

nodes.t: Isaiah sees the Lord and is sent
nodes.d: In the year King Uzziah died Isaiah sees the LORD enthroned with seraphim crying holy, is cleansed by a coal from the altar, volunteers, and is told to preach to a people who will not understand until a stump remains.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} retell Isaiah's vision in chapter 6, including what the seraphim cry and how Isaiah is cleansed?
ev: Retell what the seraphim say and do (6:2-7)
Explain Isaiah's response in 6:5 and 6:8
Describe the message he is given and the "holy seed" in 6:9-13

nodes.t: The servant, a light to the nations
nodes.d: The servant called from the womb, whose mouth is like a sharp sword, says he has laboured in vain; the LORD says it is too light a thing to restore Israel and gives him as a light to the Gentiles, and promises Zion she is not forgotten.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say what the LORD says is "too light a thing" for his servant in Isaiah 49:6?
ev: Describe how the servant is called (49:1-3)
Quote the LORD's answer in 49:6
Say what the LORD says to Zion in 49:14-16

nodes.t: The servant exalted, despised and bearing iniquity
nodes.d: The servant is high, yet marred; despised and rejected, he bears griefs and iniquities of others, is wounded for transgressions and led like a lamb, is cut off and buried with the rich, and after his soul's travail justifies many.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe what the servant suffers and for whose sake according to Isaiah 53:4-6?
ev: Describe what Isaiah 53:4-6 says he bears and for whom
Describe how he is treated (53:3, 7-9)
Say what the LORD says follows in 53:10-12

nodes.t: Come, buy without money: the sure mercies of David
nodes.d: The LORD invites the thirsty to come without money, promises an everlasting covenant, the sure mercies of David, calls the wicked to return, and says his word will accomplish what he pleases.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say who is invited and what is promised in Isaiah 55:1-7?
ev: Quote the invitation in Isaiah 55:1-3
Say what is promised to those who return (55:7)
Explain 55:10-11

nodes.t: Heaven my throne: the final word
nodes.d: The LORD asks where a house can be built for him who made all things and looks to the humble and contrite; he comforts Jerusalem, comes with fire, gathers all nations to see his glory, and the new heavens and earth remain.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} say whom the LORD looks to in Isaiah 66:2 and how the book ends?
ev: Say whom the LORD looks to (66:2)
Describe the gathering of the nations (66:18-21)
Describe the end in 66:22-24

nodes.t: Joel: overview
nodes.d: The word of the LORD to Joel: a locust plague and the near day of the LORD, a call to return with all the heart, the LORD's promise of restoration and of his Spirit poured out, and judgment on the nations.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} give a short summary of Joel and say where the 'day of the LORD' appears?
ev: Outline the book: plague (1), call and promise (2), nations judged (3)
Say what the phrase 'day of the LORD' is used for in 1:15 and 2:1

nodes.t: Restoration and the Spirit poured out
nodes.d: The LORD pities his people, drives off the northern army, restores the years the locust has eaten, and promises afterward to pour out his Spirit on all flesh, with wonders before the day of the LORD and deliverance for all who call on his name.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the promise of 2:28-29 and the promise to whoever calls on the name of the LORD?
ev: List the restoration promises of 2:19-27
Say who receives the Spirit in 2:28-29
Read the promise of 2:32

nodes.t: Amos: overview
nodes.d: Amos, a herdman of Tekoa, sees words concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah and Jeroboam: judgment on the nations and on Israel, five visions, and a closing promise to raise David's fallen tabernacle and restore Israel.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain who Amos was and what his book says about Israel in a few sentences?
ev: Outline: nations (1-2), sermons on Israel (3-6), visions (7-9)
Say what Amos was before the LORD sent him (1:1, 7:14-15)

nodes.t: Seek the LORD and live
nodes.d: Amos laments for fallen Israel, tells them to seek the LORD and not Bethel, condemns those who trample the poor and pervert justice, warns that the day of the LORD is darkness, and says the LORD hates their feasts but wants justice to roll like water.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain what the LORD says about Israel's feasts and songs and what he wants instead in Amos 5:21-24?
ev: Explain why the day of the LORD is darkness in 5:18-20
Describe what the LORD wants in 5:21-24

nodes.t: David's fallen tabernacle raised
nodes.d: The LORD promises to raise up the fallen tabernacle of David, so that Israel possess the remnant of Edom and the heathen called by his name, with abundant harvests and a restored land from which they will not be uprooted.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} describe the promises that end the book of Amos?
ev: Say what the LORD will raise up (9:11)
Describe the promises of 9:13-15

nodes.t: Habakkuk: overview
nodes.d: The burden Habakkuk saw: his complaints about violence in Judah and the LORD's answers, the vision to wait for in which the just live by faith, woes on the proud, and a prayer ending in rejoicing in the LORD.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} explain how Habakkuk moves from complaint to rejoicing?
ev: Describe the pattern of complaint and answer in chapters 1-2
Say how the book ends (3:17-19)

nodes.t: How long? The LORD raises up the Chaldeans
nodes.d: Habakkuk cries to the LORD about violence and perverted justice, and the LORD answers that he is raising up the fierce Chaldeans to sweep through the land.
nodes.q: Can {{name}} tell what Habakkuk complains about and how the LORD answers?
ev: State Habakkuk's complaint (1:2-4)
Describe the LORD's answer (1:5-11)
